values.quote: The right books in the right hands at the right time can transform a child’s world. And that’s what we believe the Soma Safari Initiative will do and in turn spark early literacy, inspire life long readers, help children across Kenya believe in their dreams and see a world full of possibilities through the stories they read

We are bringing the magic of books to children who need them most A full shipping container carrying 8,000 books and 72 free library book sharing boxes will soon arrive in Kenya. Opening doors to imagination, opportunity, and lifelong learning. In Kenya, access to books remains a challenge.
values.use_strategy: Concrete, quantified impact statement (8,000 books, 72 book-sharing boxes) paired with an access-gap framing — ideal for donor reports or press releases needing hard numbers alongside emotional appeal.

values.quote: Books, especially those which encourage young children to read with their families, promote their engagement, curiosity and natural desire to learn and hear about something new. Children will automatically engage with books that are relevant to their world, and which they have immediate access to. The receipt of this grant will put more books in children’s hands, and therefore more opportunities for families to engage with each other and promote learning in our Native cultures and environments.
values.author: Jo Williams  Zone 5 Representative, National Indian Head Start Directors Association
values.use_strategy: Links book access to family engagement and cultural relevance — supports a grant narrative on family and community literacy outcomes.
subject: Engagement
Native Culture
Cultural Preservation
Tribal Storytelling

values.quote: Growing up in a Tribal home you experience the benefits of family members telling you stories of how things happened, for example, ‘How the skunk got his tail‘ or ‘Why the possum plays dead‘. Tribal people know the benefits of storytelling to the young children in close proximity (sitting on grandma’s lap). We appreciate the efforts of UNC Greensboro in recognizing the benefits of reading to young children and wanting to get books into Tribal homes. We hope that this is only the beginning and in the future more Tribal programs will get the benefits of reading to children.
values.author: Tina Routh  President - National Indian Head Start Directors Association
values.use_strategy: Frames the program as extending an existing oral storytelling tradition into book-based literacy, emphasizing continuity rather than replacement.
